title: 02. Tool Calling & MCP: What Makes a GOOD Tool?
summary: What Makes a GOOD Tool?: explanations and runnable examples.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 ANATOMY OF A PERFECT TOOL                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  A TOOL HAS 5 PARTS:
  
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  PART 1: NAME                                              │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────    │
  │  ✅ Good: "search_web", "get_stock_price", "send_email"   │
  │  ❌ Bad:  "tool1", "do_thing", "helper"                   │
  │                                                            │
  │  Rule: Name must tell the LLM EXACTLY what it does        │
  │        LLM reads the name to decide if it should call it  │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  PART 2: DESCRIPTION                                       │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────    │
  │  ✅ Good: "Search the web for current information.        │
  │           Use for: news, facts, real-time data.           │
  │           Returns: list of results with titles & snippets"│
  │  ❌ Bad:  "Search for stuff"                              │
  │                                                            │
  │  Rule: Description is the LLM's instruction manual.       │
  │        Tell it: WHAT it does, WHEN to use it,             │
  │        WHAT it returns. More detail = better decisions.   │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  PART 3: PARAMETERS (Input Schema)                         │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────    │
  │  Each parameter needs:                                     │
  │  • type:        "string", "integer", "boolean", "array"   │
  │  • description: what this parameter means                  │
  │  • required:    is it mandatory?                           │
  │  • enum:        if only specific values allowed            │
  │  • default:     default value if not provided              │
  │                                                            │
  │  ✅ Good:                                                  │
  │  "query": {                                                │
  │    "type": "string",                                       │
  │    "description": "Search query. Be specific.             │
  │                    Example: 'Python async best practices'" │
  │  }                                                         │
  │  ❌ Bad:                                                   │
  │  "q": {"type": "string"}                                   │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  PART 4: IMPLEMENTATION (What it actually does)            │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────    │
  │  Must handle:                                              │
  │  ✅ Happy path   — normal successful execution             │
  │  ✅ Error path   — what happens when API fails             │
  │  ✅ Timeout      — don't hang forever                      │
  │  ✅ Retry logic  — transient failures                      │
  │  ✅ Validation   — bad inputs from LLM                     │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  PART 5: RETURN VALUE (What the LLM reads back)            │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────    │
  │  ALWAYS return JSON. LLMs parse JSON reliably.             │
  │                                                            │
  │  ✅ Success: {"status": "success", "result": {...}}        │
  │  ✅ Error:   {"status": "error",   "error": "...why..."}   │
  │  ✅ Empty:   {"status": "success", "result": [],           │
  │               "message": "No results found"}               │
  │                                                            │
  │  NEVER return:                                             │
  │  ❌ Raw HTML  (LLM gets confused)                          │
  │  ❌ None/null (LLM doesn't know what happened)             │
  │  ❌ Exception traceback (confuses the LLM)                 │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
